correctness.rationale: For each finite N>=3 Fourier decomposition gives bound sum s_j dot s_{j+1} >= -Nc+(1+c)|M|^2/N. Conical 3D and alternating even-XY constructions attain it, while triangle XY covers all M by complete-graph identity. For odd N>=5, equality forces z_j=A+Bt^j+Ct^{-j}; distinct Fourier frequencies 0,+/-1,+/-2 and |z_j|=1 imply B conjugate(C)=0 and B conjugate(A)+A conjugate(C)=0, leaving only pure spiral (M=0) or uniform (|M|=N), impossible for intermediate h. The odd XY Hessian Jc L and field forcing b with Lb=2(1+c)b, ||b||^2=N/2 give the precise h^2 coefficient with compactness/positive transverse gap controlling the remainder. Actual standalone check.py passed 97 tests, not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Schmidt–Luban (2002), secs. 6.3.1–6.3.2, prove the three-dimensional cycle spectral parabola and explicitly say the strict planar pentagon deficit at intermediate total spin is supported numerically but lacks rigorous proof. The new Fourier constant-modulus obstruction proves it rigorously for all odd N>=5, classifies exact parity-dependent equality at all fields, and computes previously unstated planar weak-field curvature. Konstantinidis (2014) treats odd open chains with biquadratic exchange, and Owerre–Nsofini (2015) examines anisotropic quantum-ring tunneling. Nearby retrieved mathematical results describe unrelated quantum ring entanglement, spectra, or geometric cycles; none of the retrieved claims implies the planar rigidity theorem. Historical priority is provisionally PASS, with residual risks.

value.rationale: Determines a sharp all-field spin-dimensionality obstruction for every frustrated odd classical cycle, resolving a previously numerical planar deficit for the pentagon and distinguishing it from even cycles and the triangle. Exact small-field susceptibility ratio 1/(2cos(pi/N)), including an inverse-golden-ratio pentagon and one-half asymptote, is a natural finite molecular magnetic-response invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice or restatement of the credited 3D spectral parabola.
